Appearance:

Shri Anshul Shrivastava, learned counsel for the appellan
 Ms.Priti Keshwani, learned counsel for the respondent [R-
 Order

Under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, this miscellaneous appeal is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 07.10.2023 in MACC No.1603/2021 by 20th MACT, Indore for enhancement of Rs.3 lakhs as compensation.

2. Facts in brief are that a total compensation of Rs.21,87,000/- with 6% interest from 23.08.2021 was awarded for the death of Devendra Singh Gehlot, aged 40 years and working as driver on vehicle no.MP-13-TA-4070, who died in a motor accident on 27-28/11/2020 by the negligent driving of dumper truck no.MP- 09-HH-7698 which was being driven by respondent No.1, owned by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12390 2 MA-709-2024 respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.
3.

In this appeal, only the quantum of loss of dependency is under challenge on the ground that income ought to have been assessed as Rs.15,000/- per month and Rs.250/- per day ought to have been taken into consideration while calculating the compensation.

4. Counsel for the respondent No.3 has opposed the appeal on the ground that Jaideep (NAW/2)
has not adduced documentary evidence regarding the payment of Rs.15,000/- per month to the deceased.
Mere oral statement is not reliable and tribunal has recorded cogent reasons for estimating the monthly income as Rs.10,000/- per month.

5. Heard. Perused the record.
6.

Record discloses that deceased was having driving license of heavy transport vehicle and was Smt. Aarti vs Manoj Kumar on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35738822/
1 working as a driver on a vehicle which was registered as transport vehicle.
In absence of documents the payment payable to a skilled labour ought to have been considered and that was Rs.10,500/- per month.
Besides that the tribunal ought to have taken into consideration the fact of per day allowance when the driver was out of the city on his job.
No definite figures have been produced before the tribunal, so sum of Rs.2,500/- per month is estimated as payment of allowance.
Accordingly, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12390 3 MA-709-2024 per month earning is recalculated as Rs.13,000/- (i.e. Rs.10,500+Rs.25,00).

Thus the total compensation is recalculated as under:
 Head Amount  Rs.24,57,000/-
 Loss of  dependency (i.e. Rs.13,000+40% FP=Rs.18,200 x12=2,18,40  PE=1,63,800x15=24,57,000/-)
 Loss of  Rs.2,64,000/- (i.e. Rs.44,000x6)
 consortium  Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral  Rs.16,500/-
 expenses  TOTAL Rs.27,54,000/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.27,54,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.21,87,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.5,67,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.5,67,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.3 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly.

However, for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12390 4 MA-709-2024 remaining amount the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months,
the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
